account.description: Identifier of the authenticated account the membership belongs to.

active.description: Whether the membership is active; a suspended membership is refused rather than reactivated.

source.description: The membership's source: invite when this acceptance created it, the source it already had when it was there.

sso_exempt.description: Whether the membership is exempt from SSO enforcement; an existing exemption is preserved.

tenant.description: The name of the tenant the membership was written in.

AuthnInviteInvitation.description: One invitation as the management face shows it. It never carries the acceptance token.

accepted_at.description: When the invitation was accepted, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC; null while it has not been accepted.

created_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC of issuance.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 deadline in UTC; a pending invitation at or past it can no longer be accepted.

id.description: The invitation's opaque identifier, used to revoke it.

invited_by.description: The account identifier of the issuer; empty when a host command issued the invitation without an HTTP identity.

status.description: The stored state. Expiry is not stored: an expired pending invitation still reads pending.

tenant.description: The name of the tenant the invitation grants a membership in.

AuthnInviteView.description: The answer of the acceptance read: the invitation's state, and its summary only while it can still be redeemed.

invitation.description: The invitation summary, present only for a pending invitation that can still be redeemed.

state.description: The state the read judges. Only pending carries the invitation summary: expired, accepted and revoked answer the state alone, without the invited address, the tenant's name or the deadline.

Problem.description: An RFC 9457 problem document. This is the entry point's default error shape, which a host-supplied ErrorResponder may replace.

detail.description: A longer explanation of this occurrence, present only when the answering module has one to give. It may be a sentence rendered in the request language or a language-neutral token such as "forbidden", so clients must not parse it.

instance.description: A URI identifying this occurrence; absent when there is none to give.

status.description: The HTTP status code the response is written with, repeated from the status line.

title.description: A short summary of the kind of problem. A module that sets none gets the standard English status text for the status code.

type.description: The machine-readable code identifying the kind of problem. A module that sets none gets the RFC 9457 default about:blank; codes this platform defines are URNs of the form urn:speed:<capability>:<code>.

get.description: Resolves the token's SHA-256 to an invitation and returns its view so a client can show what it is about to accept. The route is public and the token is the whole credential; the response never carries a token. An unknown token is 404. The view reflects the stored state even when the invitation can no longer be accepted, so the client should read status and expires_at rather than assume the link is redeemable.

parameters.description: The acceptance token, prefixed spd_inv_, which identifies the invitation and is the whole credential on this public route.
parameters.name: token

429.description: A send or acceptance-probe budget is spent; Retry-After names the seconds until the window opens again

Retry-After.description: The number of seconds until the counting window opens again

get.summary: Read the invitation a token points to

post.description: Redeems the invitation and writes a membership for the authenticated caller. The caller must hold the invited address as a proven email identifier; holding the link is not enough, because the inviter holds it too. When the caller has not proved it, the answer is 403 invitation-email-unproved and the client shows the proof step; the invitation stays pending. Acceptance never creates an account and never makes the invited address a sign-in identifier. A membership that already exists keeps its source and its SSO exemption; a suspended one is refused with 409 membership-inactive and the invitation is revoked. Two concurrent redemptions of one token leave at most one winner. A token that is expired, revoked or already accepted is 409.

parameters.description: The acceptance token, prefixed spd_inv_, which identifies the invitation. It grants a membership only together with an authenticated caller who proves the invited address.
parameters.name: token

schema.description: The acceptance request; only the token is read.

display_name.description: Ignored: acceptance never opens an account. Kept so an older client keeps working.

password.description: Ignored: acceptance never opens an account. Kept so an older client keeps working.

username.description: Ignored: acceptance never opens an account. Kept so an older client keeps working.

requestBody.description: The body is required but its account-opening fields are ignored; only the token is read.

400.description: The body or an argument is malformed

WWW-Authenticate.description: The capability's challenge: the Bearer and Cookie schemes, never Basic.

403.description: The caller does not hold the invited address as a proven email identifier

409.description: The caller's membership in the tenant is suspended

413.description: The request body is over the endpoint's limit

415.description: The request body is not application/json

429.description: A send or acceptance-probe budget is spent; Retry-After names the seconds until the window opens again

Retry-After.description: The number of seconds until the counting window opens again

post.summary: Redeem an invitation for the signed-in account that proves the invited address
